applies_to: a proof step closing a goal
trigger: A changed proof closes a goal or branch by several manual steps (a `rw` chain, explicit lemma applications, a hand-built term, `convert_to`, a case split) rather than by a single finishing tactic.
required: Close the goal with a standard finishing tactic, with hint lemmas if needed.
check: Replace the manual steps for that goal by a standard finishing tactic, with hints if needed (`simp`, `grind [...]`, `fun_prop`, `positivity`, `omega`, `grw [...]`, `rfl`); if it closes the goal, the original departs.

applies_to: the binders of a new declaration in a file with `variable` commands
trigger: A new declaration binds arguments in its own signature (types, instance arguments, terms) while `variable` commands in scope in that file declare arguments of the same kind.
required: Use the existing `variable`s, adding missing companions to the `variable` line, rather than rebinding them.
check: Read the `variable` commands in scope above the declaration; a departure is a signature binder duplicating one of them (same name, type or class), or a companion of one that belongs on that line.

applies_to: hypotheses and typeclass assumptions of a declaration
trigger: A new or changed declaration takes a side-condition hypothesis (nonzero, finiteness, cardinality, triviality, positivity, divisibility or membership) or a typeclass assumption that bundles more structure than the operations its statement and body mention.
required: Every hypothesis is one the proof needs, in the weakest form it needs, so the result holds in greater generality.
check: Delete the hypothesis, or replace the typeclass with the weakest class providing the operations used, and rebuild the declaration. Departure: it still compiles (perhaps after a small proof fix), or the hypothesis follows from the others by an existing lemma.

applies_to: a proof, construction or meta-code routine
trigger: A new or rewritten proof, construction or meta-code routine takes several steps of definition unfolding, element chasing, case analysis, hand-written fields or explicit loops, for a statement about notions that already have library API.
required: The result derived from existing lemmas or API (a composition, an existing equivalence or combinator) in a short proof.
check: Search the library, including recent master, for lemmas or API whose combination yields the statement (composition lemmas, existing equivalences, a general form). Departure: such a derivation exists and is shorter or needs fewer assumptions.

applies_to: `namespace`, `section`, `end` and `variable` commands
trigger: The diff adds or moves a `namespace`, `section`, `end` or `variable` command.
required: A blank line before and after the command, separating it from neighbouring declarations and commands.
check: Look at the lines directly above and below each such command. Departure: either is non-blank (another command, a declaration or a docstring) rather than the start or end of the file.

applies_to: a `simp` call in a proof
trigger: The changed proof has a `simp only [...]` or `simpa only [...]` call that closes its goal, or whose result is used only by a flexible finishing tactic tolerant of changes in goal shape (`linarith`, `nlinarith`, `omega`, `positivity`, `grind` and the like).
required: A plain `simp` or `simpa` (with only the lemmas it needs beyond the simp set), not a squeezed lemma list.
check: Look at what follows each `simp only` or `simpa only` on the same goal. Departure: nothing follows (it closes the goal), or only a flexible finishing tactic does.

applies_to: consecutive tactic calls or `calc` steps
trigger: The changed proof has consecutive tactic calls or `calc` steps of a kind one call can combine: successive rewrites at one location, a rewrite then `exact` or `assumption`, a goal-negating rewrite then `intro`, or chained `calc` steps closed alike.
required: One call doing the work: a merged rewrite list, `rwa`, `simpa ... using`, `by_contra!`, or a single `calc` step.
check: Replace the consecutive calls with one combined call (a concatenated `rw` list, `rwa` for rewrite-then-exact, `by_contra!` for negate-then-intro, one merged `calc` step) and rebuild. Departure: the combined call compiles.

applies_to: a proof step handed to `grind` or an unsqueezed `simp`
trigger: The changed code introduces `grind` or similar general automation into a proof in place of explicit steps or a term, replaces a `simp only [...]` with a bare `simp` or `simpa`, or adds tooling that suggests such replacements.
required: Keep a short explicit proof or squeezed `simp only`; use automation only where it is not markedly slower.
check: Write the explicit term or squeezed `simp only` for that step and compare elaboration time or heartbeats; a departure is that a short readable explicit form compiles, or that the automation is markedly slower (half a second counts).
not_when: The explicit proof is long or hard to read and the automation is not markedly slower.

applies_to: a file's import lines
trigger: The diff adds or changes an `import` (or `public import`) line.
required: Only imports the file needs and that none of its other imports already provides.
check: Delete the added import and rebuild the file (or run `lake exe shake`). Departure: the file still compiles, so the import is unused or arrives transitively through another import.

applies_to: the binder kind of a declaration's argument
trigger: A new declaration has an argument occurring in no later explicit argument's or hypothesis's type (only in the conclusion or instance arguments), or an argument that a later explicit argument's or hypothesis's type determines.
required: Make arguments that cannot be inferred explicit, and inferable ones implicit.
check: Read the binder kind of each such argument, including those from `variable`; a departure is an implicit binder on one that cannot be inferred, or an explicit binder on one that can.

applies_to: a short tactic proof
trigger: A changed proof is a short `by` block, a handful of tactics, made mostly of `have`, `refine`, `apply`, `exact`, `use`, `constructor` or `intro` assembling lemma applications.
required: Write the proof as a single term: a lemma application chain, anonymous constructor or `fun`.
check: Replace the `by` block with one term built from the same lemmas (dot-notation chain, `⟨…⟩`, `fun … ↦ …`); if it compiles and reads no worse, the original departs.

applies_to: the PR description or module docstring
trigger: The PR adds a new definition, structure, class or file, a lemma whose statement does not show its use, or reformulates or redesigns existing declarations.
required: Say in the module docstring or PR description why it is useful and how it will be used.
check: Read the PR description and module docstring; a departure is that neither says why the addition or change is wanted or what it is for (a downstream use, application, reference or example).

applies_to: the scope of a PR
trigger: The PR's diff contains more than one separable part: edits to a file its main change does not need, fixes unrelated to its stated purpose, or a core plus extensions or a design-heavy part that compile without each other.
required: Split separable parts into their own PRs; keep together parts that only make sense together.
check: Does the diff contain a part (a file, a section, a batch of fixes) that the rest does not depend on and that could be reviewed alone, still bundled into this PR?
not_when: The parts only make sense together, so splitting them would be arbitrary.

applies_to: a file's module docstring
trigger: The PR adds, removes, moves, renames or restates a main definition or theorem in a file with a module docstring (`/-! ... -/`), creates a file with one, or moves a declaration out of a file whose docstring may list it.
required: The module docstring covers every main definition and result the file contains, as currently stated, and claims nothing it no longer contains.
check: Compare the file's main declarations with its docstring's lists, and search other files' module docstrings for declarations the PR moved or removed. Departure: a main declaration is missing or misstated, or a docstring claims one its file no longer has.

applies_to: arguments shared by consecutive declarations
trigger: Two or more consecutive new or changed declarations take the same argument (same name and type, including instance arguments), whether in their signatures or through a `variable` line the PR edits or removes.
required: Declare the shared arguments once with `variable` (in a section) and drop them from each signature.
check: Compare the neighbouring signatures; a departure is a binder repeated in several of them, or a removed `variable` binder reappearing in each declaration, rather than declared once by `variable`.

applies_to: a proof step citing a lemma
trigger: A proof step reaches its goal indirectly: rewriting the goal or a hypothesis into another lemma's form, converting a library lemma to fit (as `rfl.le`), weakening then composing, routing through a generic instance, or opening side goals only for that adaptation.
required: The lemma whose statement is the goal, cited directly (`le_rfl`, not `rfl.le`), without the conversion.
check: Search the library (`exact?`, names the naming convention predicts for the composite or specialised statement) for a lemma whose conclusion is the step's goal as stated. Departure: one exists and closes the goal without the conversion or extra side goals.

applies_to: a declaration's statement: the types, objects and universe levels it is stated for
trigger: A new or changed declaration fixes, in its statement, a concrete type, a specific object or value, or specific universe levels (as domain, codomain, index type or parameter) where a variable carrying typeclass assumptions or hypotheses could stand.
required: State it for every type, object or value with the properties the proof actually uses.
check: Replace the concrete type, object or fixed universes by a variable assuming only the classes or hypotheses the proof uses (for universes, a typeclass hypothesis instead); if the statement and proof still compile, it departs.

applies_to: a declaration deleted, renamed or moved by the PR
trigger: The diff deletes a declaration that existed before the PR (a removed `theorem`, `lemma`, `def`, `instance` or `abbrev`), or changes its name or namespace, so that its old name would no longer resolve.
required: Keep the old name as a `@[deprecated (since := "…")]` alias or declaration pointing to its replacement.
check: For each old name that disappears, look among the PR's added lines for a `deprecated` alias or declaration carrying that name and naming its replacement; its absence shows a departure.

applies_to: line breaks in code, docstrings and comments
trigger: The diff adds a line over 100 characters, or breaks across lines a call, signature, short proof, attribute with its declaration, docstring or comment.
required: Lines of at most 100 characters; anything fitting in 100 characters stays on one line, and breaks fill lines.
check: Measure line lengths. Departure: a line exceeds 100 characters, or a broken expression, signature, docstring or comment could take its next line's leading binder, argument or word, or all of it, within 100 characters.

applies_to: a new predicate, structure, class, definition or lemma
trigger: The PR introduces a predicate, class, structure, definition or general lemma whose content is expressed entirely through notions the library already has: a standard mathematical object, a property built from existing predicates, or a basic fact about an existing operation, order or coercion.
required: No new declaration; the existing library declaration that already states or expresses it is used instead.
check: Search the library (documentation, `exact?`, names the naming convention predicts, more general forms) for a declaration stating or expressing the same thing, possibly under another name or namespace. Departure: one exists.

applies_to: arguments passed in a term or statement
trigger: The changed code passes arguments explicitly: an `@`-prefixed application with written-out arguments, a named argument `(x := e)`, or `_` or `..` placeholders in argument positions.
required: Arguments elaboration can infer are omitted: no `@`, placeholders or redundant named arguments for them.
check: Remove the `@` together with the inferable arguments and placeholders, or the named argument, and rebuild. Departure: the code still elaborates, with the same statement or proof.

applies_to: a monotonicity step in an inequality proof
trigger: A proof step proves an inequality (`≤` or `<`) from inequalities between its parts by `apply`, `refine` or `exact` of a named monotonicity or order-compatibility lemma.
required: Use `gcongr` for that step, discharging any side goals afterwards.
check: Replace the application of the named monotonicity lemma by `gcongr`, then discharge the remaining side goals; if it compiles, the original departs.

applies_to: the layout of a tactic proof
trigger: A changed tactic proof has a line holding more than one tactic, or more than one alternative of a `cases`, `induction`, `rcases` or `match`.
required: Write one tactic per line, and each alternative on its own line.
check: Look at such lines; a departure is tactics joined by `;` (not the `<;>` combinator, not inside brackets) or several `| … =>` alternatives on one line.

applies_to: a change to one member of a family of parallel declarations
trigger: The PR adds a variant of, or changes (rename, new field name, new instance, new form), one member of a family of parallel siblings: left/right or primed versions, analogous structures, simprocs, tactics, attributes, or parallel meta-code paths.
required: The same variant or change for every sibling in the family, in the same PR.
check: Identify the member's siblings (the mirrored left/right name, the analogous structure, tactic, simproc or code path) in the file and library. Departure: a sibling exists for which the PR provides no corresponding variant or change.

applies_to: the letter naming a variable or type parameter
trigger: A new binder or `variable` command introduces a letter for a type or object of a kind the file or area customarily names with particular letters (spaces, rings, algebras, ideals, submodules), or a letter resembling a digit or symbol.
required: Use the area's customary letter for that kind of object; avoid loaded or confusable letters.
check: Look up which letters the file and its area use for that kind of object; a departure is a different letter, one conventionally denoting something else there (a small real, an ideal), or one confusable with a digit.

applies_to: the name of a new lemma or definition variant
trigger: The PR adds or renames a declaration whose name is a sibling's name with a prime (`'`, `''`) appended, distinguishing it from that sibling or from a declaration it replaces.
required: A name that names the term in which the statement differs from its sibling, instead of a prime.
check: Read the new names and their siblings' statements. Departure: a name differs from its sibling only by a prime, while the statements differ in a nameable term (a structure, a hypothesis, or the form of the conclusion).
not_when: The primed declaration's docstring explains how it differs from its unprimed sibling.

applies_to: the spelling of a construct or notation within one file
trigger: The changed lines spell a construct that has interchangeable spellings (`have`/`haveI`, `=>`/`↦`, an attribute inline or on its own line, a binder named or `_`, a hyphenated or bracketed word in prose) and the construct also occurs elsewhere in the file.
required: Spell it the way the rest of the file does, in code and in docstrings.
check: Search the file for the other occurrences of the same construct; a departure is a changed line whose spelling differs from the one used by the file's other occurrences or by the neighbouring declarations.

applies_to: a cosmetic or polishing change in a PR
trigger: The PR, or a hunk of it, changes only the presentation of existing material (spacing, line breaks, wording of docstrings or comments, formatting of references) without changing meaning.
required: Leave such changes out; revert those hunks.
check: Read each such hunk; a departure is one whose only effect is spacing, wording or reference formatting and which corrects no factual or egregious error.
not_when: The change corrects an egregious error.

applies_to: a new iff lemma
trigger: The PR adds a lemma whose conclusion is an `↔` between statements about a named predicate or structure, so that each direction could be applied with dot notation, or whose directions the file uses separately.
required: Add an `alias ⟨_, _⟩ :=` of the iff, or standalone lemmas, naming each direction.
check: Search the PR and file for a named declaration proving each direction (an `alias ⟨_, _⟩` of the iff, or a standalone lemma); a departure is a useful direction with none.

applies_to: a new lemma
trigger: The PR adds a lemma whose proof only applies, specialises or chains one to three existing lemmas (a term one-liner or a short `rw`/`simp`/`ext` script), or whose statement restates a sibling or existing lemma's conclusion in an equivalent form.
required: The lemma is not added; use sites combine the existing lemmas directly, and of equivalent siblings only one is kept.
check: Does the statement give users a real simplification over combining the existing lemmas it is proved from, or is it an instantiation or reshaping that a use site gets in one line? Departure: the latter.
not_when: The statement is a real simplification over the combination of existing lemmas it replaces.

applies_to: the PR title and description
trigger: The PR's title or description names declarations, arguments, results or a kind of change (move, split, rename), or the diff moves, splits or renames code.
required: Title and description state exactly what the diff does, kept accurate as the PR changes.
check: Compare title and description with the diff; a departure is a named item absent from the diff, a claimed result the diff does not contain, a move, split or rename left undescribed, or a main subject of the diff unmentioned.

applies_to: a tactic proof
trigger: A new or golfed tactic proof packs several reasoning steps into single lines: a non-terminal `<;>`, an anonymous-constructor `refine` with nested `by` blocks, merged `obtain`s without type ascriptions, or one long automation call (with many hints) carrying an intricate argument.
required: Intermediate steps that read on their own: `have`s with stated types, `calc` blocks, separate bullets, type ascriptions kept.
check: Can a reader without the infoview follow each step, seeing the intermediate claims (stated `have` types, `calc` lines, ascriptions), or is the substance hidden in merged steps, a non-terminal `<;>` or opaque automation? Departure: the latter.
not_when: A shortening that removes redundant steps rather than merging them, leaving each remaining step readable.

applies_to: a universally quantified statement, hypothesis or structure field
trigger: A statement, hypothesis or structure field quantifies a variable (`∀ x, P x → …` or `∀ x ∈ s, …`) and the hypothesis immediately following the binder mentions that variable, so determines it.
required: Bind it strict-implicitly: `∀ ⦃x⦄, x ∈ s → …`.
check: Read the binder; a departure is an explicit `∀ x,` or the binder notation `∀ x ∈ s,` rather than `∀ ⦃x⦄,`.

applies_to: a third party's edit to existing code or prose
trigger: The PR alters existing code, docstrings or comments only stylistically (rewording, punctuation, dash style, heading levels, notation formatting), leaving the meaning unchanged.
required: Leave it as the original author wrote it; revert the stylistic change.
check: Is each such change required by the style guide, or does it fix a spelling, grammar or factual error? If neither, it departs.
not_when: The style guide mandates it, the original had a real error, or the original author agrees.

applies_to: a proof's dependencies and the file the lemma sits in
trigger: A new proof uses a construction or lemma not available in the earliest file where the statement's notions are defined, or the PR adds imports that the proof needs but the statement does not.
required: Prove it from what is available where the statement makes sense, and place it in that earliest file.
check: Could the statement be proved by elementary means available where its notions are defined, avoiding the heavier lemma, construction or import, so that it could sit in an earlier file?

applies_to: a hand-written dual, additive, projection or characterisation lemma
trigger: The PR hand-writes a declaration of a kind a generator produces: the order-dual or additive version of a neighbouring lemma, a projection or component lemma of a definition built with structure syntax, or an iff unfolding a structure or class into its fields.
required: Generate it with `to_dual`, `to_additive`, `simps` or `mk_iff`, placing the source after the lemmas the generator needs.
check: Delete the hand-written lemma and put the generator attribute (`to_dual`, `to_additive`, `simps`, `mk_iff`) on its source, moving the source after the lemmas it needs if necessary; if the generated statement serves and everything compiles, it departs.

applies_to: a name ending in a prime
trigger: The changed code declares, renames or refers to a declaration, structure field or `to_additive` target name ending in a prime (`'`).
required: An unprimed name, unless an unprimed sibling exists that is the primary form.
check: Search the library and the PR for the same name without the prime. Departure: no declaration or field with the unprimed name exists, so the prime distinguishes nothing.

applies_to: the PR title
trigger: The pull request has a title (always true: the convention concerns the title of every PR).
required: A title `type(Area): description`, type a keyword such as feat, fix, chore, refactor, doc or perf, Area the edited path.
check: Read the title. Departure: it lacks a lowercase type keyword, a parenthesised area naming the edited directory or file (without `Mathlib/` and `.lean`), or a colon followed by a description.

applies_to: placement of a declaration's term-mode proof
trigger: A new or changed declaration has a term-mode proof (not a `by` block) written after `:=` on the same line as the last line of its statement.
required: The proof on its own indented line, unless the whole declaration, statement and proof together, fits on one line.
check: Look at the declaration's lines. Departure: the statement occupies more than one line, or the single line exceeds 100 characters, yet the proof term follows `:=` on the statement's line.

applies_to: a new declaration's name and namespace
trigger: A new declaration is a variant, special case or counterpart of an existing one (the same statement on another type, the symmetric or reversed case, an analogous construction), or its name uses a standard part such as a hypothesis abbreviation or a positional affix.
required: Name and place it as its siblings and analogues are: same abbreviations, part order, affix position and namespace.
check: Find the siblings or analogues (neighbouring declarations, the general lemma in the library, the counterpart construction) and compare names; a departure is a part spelled more fully or differently, parts in another order, or another namespace for the same kind of construction.

applies_to: a new declaration about a multiplicative or additive algebraic structure
trigger: The PR adds a definition, lemma or instance whose statement involves a multiplicative structure or operation (`*`, `⁻¹`, `1`, monoid- or group-style classes and bundled maps), or an additive one (`+`, `-`, `0`, additive classes).
required: Its counterpart exists: `@[to_additive]` on the multiplicative declaration where that works, otherwise a hand-written counterpart beside it.
check: Read whether the declaration carries `@[to_additive]`. If not, search the PR and the library for the counterpart (name and statement with mul/add, one/zero, inv/neg swapped). Departure: neither the attribute nor a counterpart exists.
not_when: The declaration is additive and its statement has no multiplicative analogue.

applies_to: the layout of parallel one-line declarations
trigger: The changed code contains two or more one-line declarations of parallel form near each other: counterpart lemmas, aliases of corresponding directions, or dual statements.
required: Put them on consecutive lines with no blank line between, so the parallel lines up.
check: Read the layout; a departure is a blank line or an interposed declaration between parallel one-line declarations of the same shape.

applies_to: a docstring's prose
trigger: A new or changed docstring uses an identifier abbreviation (`hom`, `add`, `mul`) or an undefined shorthand as an English word, or names a mathematical object by a pasted Lean expression (an application or dot-notation term) instead of words.
required: Write full mathematical words (homomorphism, additive monoid) and describe objects in prose.
check: Read the docstring's prose; a departure is an identifier abbreviation or shorthand used as a word, or a Lean term in backticks standing where a phrase describing the object would do.

applies_to: attributes of a new characterisation lemma
trigger: The PR adds a lemma whose conclusion is an `↔` or an `=` characterising a predicate or operation in terms of other notions (a `..._iff` lemma, or an equation unfolding or computing a definition).
required: The lemma tagged `@[grind =]`, alongside any other attributes it carries.
check: Check whether it carries a `grind` attribute; if not, add `@[grind =]` and build. Departure: no `grind` attribute is present and `@[grind =]` is accepted (grind finds a usable pattern on the left-hand side).

applies_to: changes to existing declarations in a PR
trigger: The diff changes the proof, body or name of a declaration that existed before the PR (removed lines replaced by new ones), rather than only adding code.
required: Existing code changed only where the PR's purpose requires; other proofs and names left as they were.
check: Restore the pre-PR proof or name (with its uses) and rebuild against the rest of the PR. Departure: it still compiles and the PR's description does not make that change part of its purpose.
not_when: The change is what the PR is for, or the old code stops compiling after the PR's other changes.

applies_to: section and `variable` organisation of typeclass assumptions
trigger: The PR adds an `omit` command, or adds or strengthens typeclass assumptions on a `variable` line shared by several declarations of a section.
required: Separate sections, each declaring exactly the assumptions its declarations need; no `omit`.
check: Look for `omit` in the changed sections, and for a section assumption that some declarations in its scope do not use. Departure: either is present.

applies_to: the generality of a new or changed declaration
trigger: A new or changed declaration is stated beyond the standard case: semilinear maps or an extra ring hom `σ`, additional type or ring parameters, coefficients beyond the usual fields, or a weakened structure in a core definition.
required: The statement in the generality existing uses need; it is generalised when a use arrives.
check: Search the PR and the library for uses that need the extra generality (a non-identity `σ`, the other parameters or coefficients, the weaker structure). Departure: none exist, and the generality adds arguments, hypotheses or friction (lost notation, harder statements).
not_when: The general form is no more complicated to state or use than the special one.

applies_to: a declaration introduced with the `theorem` keyword
trigger: The PR adds a declaration using the `theorem` keyword.
required: Give it a docstring, or use `lemma` if it is an auxiliary result.
check: Look immediately above the `theorem` and its attributes for a `/-- … -/` docstring; its absence shows a departure.
not_when: The `theorem` is pre-existing code that the PR merely edits.

applies_to: the spelling of a hypothesis, conclusion or assumption
trigger: A new statement phrases a hypothesis, conclusion or typeclass assumption in one of several equivalent spellings the library has: set-level versus elementwise, membership versus (in)equality, one of several equivalent classes, or one construction versus another.
required: The spelling most existing library lemmas use; if another is kept, lemmas relating the two spellings.
check: Search the library for lemmas about the same notions and see which spelling most use. Departure: the new statement uses a less common spelling and the PR adds no lemma converting it to the common one.

applies_to: a `variable` command and its section
trigger: The PR adds a `variable` command (including `variable ... in`), opens a section to hold one, or adds binders to an existing one.
required: `variable` only for arguments shared by many declarations; arguments of one or a few declarations bound in their signatures.
check: For each binder of the `variable` command, count the declarations in its scope that use it. Departure: some binder is used by only one or a few declarations, or by none.

applies_to: a hypothesis binder whose type is a class
trigger: A declaration takes a hypothesis whose type is a typeclass applied to arguments, such as `IsEmpty α`, `Nonempty α`, `Fact p` or any other declared `class`.
required: Take it as an instance-implicit argument `[C x]`.
check: Read the binder; a departure is a named explicit or implicit binder `(h : C x)` or `{h : C x}` instead of `[C x]`.

applies_to: a proof step closing a goal with a lemma
trigger: A proof rewrites the goal backwards (`rw [← ...]`, `nth_rw ... [← ...]`, `simp only [← ...]`) to put it into the form of a lemma that it then `apply`s or `exact`s.
required: `simpa using` the lemma, with its arguments (implicit ones too) supplied explicitly, letting `simp` normalise into the goal.
check: Replace the backward rewrites and the closing `apply` or `exact` with `simpa using L ...`, giving L's arguments explicitly (named arguments for implicit ones), and rebuild. Departure: it compiles.
